tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List recorded sessions, newest first: id, app, device, transaction and error counts. Use this to find a session id; 'latest' always works without calling it.

tools.name: session_summary
tools.description: Compact digest of one session: counts by status class and host, the slowest calls, every error, and the marker labels. About a kilobyte. Start here — it answers most questions without reading any transactions.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.description: Transactions matching a filter, newest first. Bodies are NOT included; call get_body for those. Filter grammar: status:404, status>=400, method:POST, host:api.example.com, path:/v2/users, slower:500ms, larger:10kb, has:error, text:refund, attempt>1, since:marker("label"). Terms separated by spaces are ANDed; '|' ORs.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Default 25, maximum 200.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

tools.name: get_transaction
tools.description: One transaction in full, including every header. Bodies are referenced but not inlined; call get_body for those.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

id.description: Transaction id, as returned by list_transactions.

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Everything the archive knows about one call, joined: the screen the app was on and how long it had been there, the other attempts of the same call, the calls that were in flight at the same moment, how often the same endpoint was hit, and the signals either side of it. Use this instead of get_transaction when the question is 'why' rather than 'what' — it is one call where the alternative is four and the joins done by hand.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

id.description: Transaction id, as returned by list_transactions.

windowMs.description: How far either side to look for context, in device ms. Default 5000, maximum 60000.

tools.name: get_body
tools.description: The captured request or response body of one transaction. Truncated by default because bodies are large and context is not.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

tools.name: route_stats
tools.description: Per-route latency and failure stats for one session, computed from every call in it. A route is a path template: numeric, UUID, long hex and long base64-like segments read as {id}, and routeTemplates in the daemon's config.json overrides that. One row per method, host and route: calls, attempts (each redirect hop or retry is an attempt), retries, 4xx/5xx/transport-failure rates over attempts with an outcome, and p50/p90/p95/p99/max ms over attempts that got a response. p95 and p99 are omitted with tailWithheld "n<20" below 20 samples; transport failures never count toward latency. Each row's filterTerm, passed to list_transactions, returns a superset of that row's calls: the filter grammar cannot say a route exactly. sort: attempts (default), p50, p90, p95, p99, max, errors.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

filter.description: Filter expression, as list_transactions takes it; only matching calls are counted. Empty counts every call.

sort.description: Row order, descending, rows with no value last. Default 'attempts'.

limit.description: Maximum routes to return. Default 25, maximum 200; routeCount says how many there are.

tools.name: list_findings
tools.description: Findings for one session: what the daemon's rules flag in its calls, computed from every call each time it is asked and never written to the archive. Each finding has ruleId, category, severity (high, medium or info), route, message, txnIds and callIds (pass a txnId to get_transaction; txnCount says how many there are when txnIds is cut at 200), and evidence lines, each about one txnId, with an optional location, path and masked hint. Nothing in a finding is a captured value: request bodies are compared but never shown, and a body capture did not keep reads "body unknown". rules lists every rule checked with its count, so count 0 means checked and found nothing; enabled false means config.json's findings key turned it off. coverage says, per category, what could not be judged. Payment rules look only at POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. The findings settings in config.json are read on every call, so this tool and the web page agree; ruleVersion names the settings an answer was computed under, and configError says when the file's findings key could not be read and the last good settings were used. Values are never returned, only a masked hint. Dismissed findings (set aside with a reason in config.json's findingDismissals; no tool can dismiss one) are left out unless includeDismissed, and dismissedCount says how many there are; a dismissed finding carries dismissed.reason.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

category.description: Only this category's rules and findings. Absent means every category.

limit.description: Maximum findings to return. Default 50, maximum 200; findingCount says how many there are.

includeDismissed.description: Also list dismissed findings, each with its reason. Default false.

tools.name: timeline
tools.description: Transactions, signals and markers merged by the device clock, oldest first, one compact line each. This is the tool that answers 'what was the app doing when this failed' — start from a marker and read forwards. Follow an id into get_signal or get_body for detail. Same filter grammar as list_transactions plus tag: and name:. Same-millisecond ties follow the shared timeline rule: a marker comes before the call or signal at its instant.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

since.description: Only entries at or after this device mono (ms).

until.description: Only entries at or before this device mono (ms).

tools.name: current
tools.description: The latest observation per (tag, name), with how old each one is. One call answers 'what screen was the app on, what was cached'. Read 'trigger' before reporting any of it as live: 'app' means the app pushed it at that moment and has not re-read it since — a snapshot from app start is not the current state. 'request' means it was pulled fresh. Use request_signal to get a genuinely current value.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

tag.description: Restrict to one tag, e.g. 'cache'. Optional.

tools.name: list_signals
tools.description: Signals matching a filter, newest first. Payloads are NOT included; call get_signal for those. Filter terms for signals: tag:screen (exact), name:Checkout (substring), text:refund (tag and name, never payloads), since:marker("label"). Transaction-only terms such as status: match no signals at all, so 'status:500 tag:screen' returns nothing — use '|' to span both kinds. Payloads are NOT redacted even when the session was recorded with redaction on.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Default 25, maximum 200.

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. Default 0.

tools.name: get_signal
tools.description: One signal in full, with its payload, truncated by default. Check 'trigger': 'app' was pushed by the app at that moment, 'request' was pulled on demand. Signal payloads are app state, captured verbatim and NOT redacted — they may contain credentials or customer data even in a session recorded with redaction on.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

id.description: Signal id, as returned by list_signals or timeline.

maxBytes.description: Truncate the payload beyond this. Default 8192.

tools.name: request_signal
tools.description: Ask the running app what it holds right now, rather than reading what it pushed earlier. Requires a live session with an attached app and a provider registered for that tag and name; both failures are reported explicitly, and the error names which providers do exist.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

name.description: Provider name within the tag, e.g. 'response'.

tools.name: add_marker
tools.description: Drop a labelled marker into the timeline of the session that is recording right now, so later calls can be filtered with since:marker("label"). Requires a running daemon.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

tools.name: export_session
tools.description: Write one whole session to files a person can open: HTML (the web UI, working offline from disk, with every call, body, signal and marker), Markdown (the timeline, then every call's request and response in full) and JSON (everything in one document). Returns the paths. Use it to hand a session to someone; to read one yourself, the other tools are cheaper.

session.description: Session id, or 'latest' for the most recent. Defaults to 'latest'.

dir.description: Directory to write into, created if missing. Default: the 'exports' folder beside the archive's sessions.
